body: ## The town with the most empty units

Of Sherborn's 1,632 housing units, 1,511 are occupied and 121 are vacant. That works out to a 7.4% vacancy rate according to the Census Bureau's 2022 American Community Survey (ACS 2022), the highest of the 50 towns Mass HVAC serves and more than double the 3.6% of the middle town. The survey does not say why a unit is empty, so the number tells us only that more of the housing here than anywhere else in our area sits unoccupied at the time of the count.

A vacant house still has a heating system, and a general rule applies to any of them: an unoccupied building in winter needs its heat kept at a safe minimum, because frozen pipes cause damage whether or not anyone lives inside.
## Oil heat, and almost no bottled gas

Fuel oil or kerosene heats 994 occupied homes, 65.8%, which ranks 5th of 50 and sits far above the 36.5% of the middle town. Utility gas serves 334 homes (22.1%), 38th. Electricity heats 107 (7.1%), 43rd. At the other end, bottled or tank gas heats just 16 homes (1.1%), the 50th and lowest share of all.

Those numbers draw a clear line for a replacement decision. A Sherborn owner with an oil boiler is rarely choosing between oil and propane, since propane is nearly absent. The real comparison is a new oil unit, gas where a main reaches the house, or a heat pump. Houses with an oil tank also raise a practical point: any replacement is a chance to ask how old the tank is and whether it still belongs in the plan.
## Mostly built before 1980

The median Sherborn home dates from 1969, which ranks 15th-oldest of 50, against 1975 for the middle town. In all, 1,179 units (72.2%) were built before 1980, the 4th-highest share. The biggest single band is 1960 to 1979 with 674 units (41.3%). Another 303 units (18.6%) are from 1939 or earlier, 202 (12.4%) from 1940 to 1959 and 296 (18.1%) from 1980 to 1999. Only 157 (9.6%) are from 2000 or later.

Houses in that spread of decades carry very different amounts of insulation and air leakage. Before quoting a system, we assess the home's heating load, so the capacity follows the house instead of the unit being removed.
## Eighteen miles from Boston, shared schools with Dover

Sherborn sits in Boston's MetroWest region, 18 miles southwest of Boston, with area code 508 and ZIP Code 01770. It borders Dover, Natick, Framingham, Ashland, Millis, Holliston and Medfield. The town covers 16.2 square miles, of which 16.0 are land and 0.2 are water (1.36%), much of it in Farm Pond.

Sherborn shares its public school system with Dover, a neighbor on the town's border. Its own elementary school is Pine Hill School, and most middle and high school students attend Dover-Sherborn schools located in Dover.
## Rebates depend on the address

Our data does not confirm an electric utility for Sherborn. Sherborn's electric utility is not confirmed in our data, and rebates follow the utility that serves each address. The [heat pump page](/cities/sherborn/heat-pumps-ductless-mini-splits) shows how the program meets an older housing stock. Confirm current terms at masssave.com before you set a budget, since they can change from one year to the next.

faq.q: Is Sherborn's vacancy rate really the highest in the area?
faq.a: Yes. The 2022 survey counts 121 vacant units out of 1,632, or 7.4%, the highest among the 50 towns Mass HVAC serves. The middle town is at 3.6%. The survey does not explain individual cases, so treat it only as a measure of how many units were empty when households were counted.

faq.q: Should I replace a Sherborn oil boiler with a heat pump?
faq.a: It depends on the house, but the question comes up often, since oil heats 65.8% of occupied homes here. A heat pump can heat and cool, and rebates may apply, but the home usually needs to be weatherized first and the system sized correctly. Propane is rare in Sherborn, so the comparison is mostly oil, gas or a heat pump.

faq.q: Does the age of Sherborn houses change the right system size?
faq.a: It can change it a lot. With a median build year of 1969 and 72.2% of units built before 1980, many houses have gone through different generations of insulation and windows. Copying the capacity of the old boiler can overshoot or undershoot, so we assess the home's heating load before we quote.

faq.q: Which utility affects my heat pump rebate?
faq.a: Whichever company supplies power to the house, and our data does not name it for Sherborn. Rebate rules differ by utility, and terms can change. Check your electric bill for the utility name, then confirm the current program at masssave.com or with the utility before you commit to a budget.

heating-installation-repair.quickAnswer: Beyond oil, 334 Sherborn homes use utility gas (22.1%, 38th of 50), 107 use electricity (7.1%) and 53 burn wood (3.5%). A heating swap usually means weighing oil, gas and electric against one another.
body: ## What heats the other third

Oil dominates Sherborn, but about a third of occupied homes use something else. The 2022 American Community Survey (ACS 2022) counts 334 homes on utility gas (22.1%), which ranks 38th of 50. Electricity heats 107 homes (7.1%), ranking 43rd. Wood heats 53 homes (3.5%), and 7 homes use another fuel such as coal.
That mix means three replacement stories. A gas house replaces gas equipment. An electric house may look at a heat pump. And an owner on oil looks at everything.
### Gas conversion and permits

Utility gas is available only where a main reaches the house, and the gas company decides that. A gas furnace or boiler swap normally comes with a permit and a final inspection, and Massachusetts reserves gas permits for licensed plumbers and gas fitters. Ask the building department which local steps follow.
### Houses from earlier eras

The town has 303 units from 1939 or earlier (18.6%), ranked 19th of 50, and 202 from 1940 to 1959 (12.4%). Insulation and windows in houses that old can differ widely from one to the next, so the capacity of the old boiler is a weak guide. Replacement equipment can be sized from a heating load assessment, which we do before quoting.
### Rentals

Rentals are a small group here: 117 households (7.7%), ranking 46th. For those tenants, the sanitary code sets a floor during the heating season: 68 F in the daytime window and 64 F overnight, with heat paid by the landlord unless the lease differs. That is general information, not legal advice.
### Emergencies

Call (508) 786-8755 at any hour. Mass HVAC is licensed and insured, takes emergency calls day and night, and provides a free written estimate before work starts. A repair that turns into a full replacement gets the same written estimate, so the choice is on paper before you commit. For upkeep after a replacement, see the [maintenance page](/cities/sherborn/hvac-maintenance-tune-ups).

faq.q: Can a Sherborn home on oil switch to utility gas?
faq.a: Only when a gas main reaches the property or can be extended to it, and that is the gas company's call. About one in five Sherborn homes (22.1%) already use utility gas, so lines exist in parts of town. Where none is available, the choices are another oil system or a heat pump.

faq.q: What if my boiler stops working on a weekend?
faq.a: Call (508) 786-8755, because emergency calls are taken around the clock. While you wait, check the thermostat and the circuit breaker, and keep the house warm enough to protect the pipes. The free written estimate for any repair or replacement arrives before work begins.

faq.q: Do older Sherborn houses need a bigger boiler?
faq.a: Not necessarily. Older houses can lose more heat, but upgrades since the original build can change the picture, so size is better set by a heating load assessment than by a rule of thumb or the old nameplate. With 18.6% of units from 1939 or earlier, the range of conditions in town is wide.

air-conditioning-installation-repair.quickAnswer: Detached houses are 90.3% of Sherborn housing (6th of 50) and the median owner-occupied home is worth $898,900. Cooling projects are mostly a detached-house story, with ductless heads an option where ducts are limited.
body: ## A town of single-family houses

The 2022 American Community Survey (ACS 2022) counts 1,473 single-family detached houses among Sherborn's 1,632 units, or 90.3%, the 6th-highest share of the 50 towns. The remaining housing is small: 50 townhouse units (3.1%), 11 units in two-unit buildings (0.7%), 45 in buildings of three or four units (2.8%) and 53 in buildings of five or more (3.2%). All multi-unit buildings together hold 109 units, 6.7%, which ranks 44th.
The median owner-occupied home is valued at $898,900, 8th-highest of 50 and well above the $579,150 of the middle town.
### What detached houses allow

A detached house has exterior walls on every side, which gives an installer choices for placing condensers and routing lines. A condo or an apartment block has fewer. With roughly nine in ten Sherborn homes detached, those choices are widely available in principle, though each lot and house still has its own limits.
### Central air, ductless or both

Central air needs ductwork in good condition, sized for cooling airflow. Ductless mini-splits avoid ducts and cool one zone at a time. A mix, with central air serving the main floors and a ductless head covering a far corner or an upstairs room, is a common compromise.
### How age shapes the cooling load

Sherborn has 98 units built since 2010 (6.0%), ranking 36th, and 157 built in 2000 or later (9.6%). Newer houses tend to be built tighter and with better windows, which lowers the load to be cooled. Older houses can be harder to cool evenly. Either way, sizing from the house, not from habit, matters: an air conditioner that is too large turns off before it removes enough moisture.
### Repairs

Small faults, such as a failed capacitor or a dirty coil, are generally fixable. A failed compressor on equipment that has run for many years usually leads to a replacement conversation. The estimate for either route is written and free, and it arrives before work starts.
### Heat pumps for cooling

A heat pump cools in summer and heats in winter, so some owners compare it against a stand-alone air conditioner. Rebate details are on our [heat pump page](/cities/sherborn/heat-pumps-ductless-mini-splits).

faq.q: Can I add cooling to a Sherborn house with baseboard heat?
faq.a: Yes. Hot-water baseboard heat has no ducts, so cooling usually means ductless mini-splits, or a small ducted system in an attic or basement if there is room. Which one fits depends on the layout. With 90.3% of town housing detached, most houses have exterior walls available for the outdoor unit.

faq.q: Does a bigger air conditioner cool better?
faq.a: No. An oversized unit cools quickly, shuts off before the air is dehumidified and leaves a clammy house. It also cycles more often, which wears parts. The better target is a unit whose capacity matches the load of the house, which is why sizing starts with the building and not with the old nameplate.

faq.q: Should I repair or replace an aging air conditioner?
faq.a: Repair a small part, replace when a major component fails on old equipment or when repairs keep recurring. A written estimate should show the repair price next to the replacement price so you can compare. With the median home valued at $898,900, the choice is worth weighing carefully.

heat-pumps-ductless-mini-splits.quickAnswer: Only 157 Sherborn units (9.6%) date from 2000 or later, so most owners meet the Mass Save weatherization test through an assessment rather than by build year. The program that applies turns on who supplies your electricity.
body: ## An older housing stock meets the weatherization test

The 2026 whole-home Mass Save rebate pays $2,650 per ton, capped at $8,500, once the house is weatherized enough. Everything else about it sits on the [statewide heat pump page](/services/heat-pumps-ductless-mini-splits).

A house built in 2000 or later passes that test automatically, and Sherborn has 157 such units. At the other end, 1,179 units were built before 1980 (72.2%), and the largest group, 674 units, comes from 1960 to 1979. Those houses go through an assessment instead, and the program's own conditions decide the result.
### Utility first
Sherborn's electric utility is not confirmed in our data, so which program pays you comes down to the name on your electric bill. Terms can change.
### Who is switching from what

Oil heats 994 Sherborn homes (65.8%), electricity heats 107, and bottled gas heats only 16. For an oil household, a heat pump replaces a delivered fuel with electricity for part or all of the year. The comparison with propane almost never arises, because so few homes use it. Utility gas serves 334 homes, where the comparison is between two fuels that both have a monthly bill.
### Partial or whole

An owner who wants to keep a working boiler can pair it with a heat pump for the mild months. That is a partial-home setup, with its own smaller rebate per ton. A whole-home setup retires the old plant. Both depend on the weatherization and sizing steps.
### Houses with no ducts

Ductless heads are a practical route when a house has hot-water radiators or baseboard. A ducted system suits a house with good ducts. In both cases, we assess the home's heating load before quoting and put the options in a free written estimate.
### Cooling too

Because a heat pump also cools, it can retire an old air conditioner at the same time. Our [cooling page](/cities/sherborn/air-conditioning-installation-repair) covers the town's mostly detached housing.

faq.q: Is a 1969 Sherborn house too old for a heat pump?
faq.a: No. Age affects the weatherization step, not eligibility for the technology. The median Sherborn home dates from 1969, so the usual route is a Home Energy Assessment. If it recommends under $1,000 of work, or earlier recommendations were completed, the house can pass. Check masssave.com, because terms can change.

faq.q: Will a heat pump replace my oil boiler completely?
faq.a: It can in a well-sealed, properly sized house, but many owners keep the boiler for the coldest days. With oil in 65.8% of Sherborn homes, the partial-home route is worth a look. Which setup fits depends on the heating load assessment and on what the rebate rules allow at your address.

faq.q: Does a heat pump make sense in a house with an oil tank in the basement?
faq.a: It can. A heat pump can take over part or all of the heating, and the oil tank then runs down more slowly or is retired. The 994 oil-heated homes in Sherborn, 65.8% of the total, are the group for whom that question is most live. A heating load assessment gives the size, and the rebate path follows your utility.

hvac-maintenance-tune-ups.quickAnswer: Oil is the main fuel in Sherborn (994 homes, 65.8%), and owners hold 92.3% of households. For most systems here, the maintenance question is the oil burner's yearly cleaning, plus a plan for houses that stay empty.
body: ## Oil, owners and a yearly routine

Oil heats 994 Sherborn homes, the 5th-highest share of the 50 towns. Oil equipment needs a cleaning every year: the technician removes soot, replaces the filter and nozzle, and checks combustion. That is the core of the maintenance season in town.
### Who books the visit

The 2022 American Community Survey (ACS 2022) counts 1,394 owner-occupied households (92.3%) and 117 renter households (7.7%, 46th of 50). In an owner-occupied house, whoever owns it also decides when the boiler is serviced. In a rental, the landlord normally pays for heat unless the lease says otherwise, and a tune-up before the heating season is one way a landlord reduces the chance of a failure in a cold snap.
### Gas and electric equipment

Gas serves 334 homes and electricity serves 107. A gas burner needs a safety and combustion check on its burner, venting and controls. A heat pump or electric system has no flame, but coils, filters and condensate drains still need attention.
### Empty houses

Sherborn's 121 vacant units make for the highest vacancy rate in our area, 7.4%. A home that stands empty for part of the year can use a different checklist: set the thermostat to a safe minimum in winter, ask someone to look in on it, and have the system checked before the family or a new owner returns.
### Old houses, old equipment

The town has 303 units from 1939 or earlier and 674 from 1960 to 1979. Equipment that has run for many years can develop faults, and a planned visit can find a failing part early, such as a cracked heat exchanger or a clogged nozzle, instead of discovering it on the coldest night of the year.
### Seasonal timing
- **Late summer to early fall:** heating checks, ahead of the first cold nights.
- **Spring:** cooling checks for central air and ductless systems.
- **Anytime:** short cycling, a burning smell or a spike in bills.
See the [heating page](/cities/sherborn/heating-installation-repair) if a check turns into a replacement.

faq.q: What does an oil burner cleaning in Sherborn include?
faq.a: The technician removes soot, replaces the filter and nozzle, and checks combustion. Doing it before the heating season starts helps keep the burner efficient and lowers the chance of a breakdown in the coldest weeks. With 65.8% of Sherborn homes on oil, this is the standard annual service in town.

faq.q: Should I have a vacant house serviced?
faq.a: If it will sit empty, yes, ideally before it does. Heat set to a safe minimum, an inspection of the system, and a periodic check by someone you trust all reduce the risk of frozen pipes or a failed boiler going unnoticed. Sherborn's 7.4% vacancy rate is the highest of the 50 towns.

faq.q: How do I know a tune-up is overdue?
faq.a: Signs include short cycling, new noises, smells, uneven rooms, and bills that rise while your habits stay the same. A missed annual cleaning on an oil burner is the most common reason for trouble. If you cannot remember the last service date, treat it as overdue and book before the heating season.

indoor-air-quality.quickAnswer: Sherborn's 1,179 pre-1980 units (72.2%) and 157 units from 2000 or later make for very different air. Older houses often leak, newer ones hold moisture, and the right response starts with a measurement.
body: ## Two kinds of houses, two kinds of air

According to the 2022 American Community Survey (ACS 2022), 72.2% of Sherborn units were built before 1980, ranking 4th of 50, while 9.6% date from 2000 or later. The two ends of that range behave differently indoors.
### Older houses

Houses from before 1980 often leak air around windows, sills and chimneys. That dilutes some pollutants, but it also lets in dust, pollen and damp basement air. If renovation is planned in an older house, a qualified specialist should test for older materials such as lead paint or asbestos before work begins. That is general advice, not a finding about any Sherborn property.
### Tighter houses

A house built in 2000 or later is usually tighter. That saves energy, and it can also keep moisture, cooking fumes and chemicals inside unless ventilation does its job. A ventilator that exchanges stale and fresh air is the usual remedy.
### Oil and combustion

Because 994 homes burn oil, combustion air quality deserves a mention. Soot from a poorly tuned burner can reach the living space, and a leaking flue can release carbon monoxide. Detectors are inexpensive and are worth having wherever fuel is burned, and they are a sensible habit in any house, whether the house is old or new.
### Humidity and the seasons

Heated winter air tends to be dry, and summer brings humidity back. A basement in an older house can run damp. Measuring first shows which problem you actually have, and a humidifier, dehumidifier or ventilator then answers that problem rather than a guess.
### Water nearby
Water covers 1.36% of Sherborn, much of it in Farm Pond. Proximity to water does not by itself say anything about a given house, so a damp-basement concern should be measured inside that house.
### Testing and fixing

Air testing is a snapshot. Fixing the source, whether a leaking duct, an unvented appliance or a wet basement, keeps the result. For equipment care that supports air quality, see the [maintenance page](/cities/sherborn/hvac-maintenance-tune-ups).

faq.q: Do old houses in Sherborn have worse indoor air?
faq.a: Not automatically. With 303 units built in 1939 or earlier (18.6%), plenty of houses leak air, which brings in dust and damp air but also dilutes other pollutants. The better question is what the house contains and how it is ventilated, and testing answers that more reliably than age does.

faq.q: When should I test my indoor air?
faq.a: Test when you have a symptom or a suspicion: a musty smell, condensation on windows, headaches that fade away from home, or a plan for renovation in an older house. Testing before and after a fix shows whether the fix worked. Remember that one test is only a snapshot of one day.

They can help with particles, but they do not fix moisture, combustion gases or a leaking duct. Removing or controlling the source is the lasting answer. Purifiers work best beside ventilation, filter changes and humidity control, not as a replacement for them.
